native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital (Copper & Gold + Amber + Monument Count, simple sum of raw Z) peaks in the Late Bronze Age in the 13th century BCE, i.e. the 1300-1201 BCE bin (3250-3151 calBP; CE signed -1300 to -1201); the adjacent 1400-1301 BCE bin (3350-3251 calBP) is exactly tied, so the safest phrasing is a peak spanning 1400-1201 BCE, best single century 1300-1201 BCE, which wins outright under 150/200/250-year smoothing (3 of 5 windows) and is identical in capital.csv, the raw anchors of time_series_data.csv and its annual interpolated grid. The individual social-capital components that increase are Copper & Gold (ZCU_AU: Z=+2.54, 95th percentile, 59.9% of the peak anomaly, positive 500-year trend) and Monument Count (ZMonument: Z=+1.71, 97th percentile, 40.3% of the anomaly, positive trend); together they account for essentially 100% of the peak anomaly (+4.238 exact additive decomposition). Amber (Zamber) does NOT increase: Z=-0.01 at the peak, -0.3% of the anomaly, its own maximum lying in 3300-3000 BCE with a negative long-run trend. The peak is social-specific in the 13th-century bin: cultural capital (pottery form/decoration diversity) is below its mean (28th of 39 bins) and economic capital (Depot, Sickle, Axes & Celts, Monument Size) is below its mean (34th of 39), while only symbolic capital (Hatchets & Swords, Daggers, House Size) is simultaneously high (2nd of 39) although its own maximum lies two centuries later (1800-1701 BCE); in the tied 14th-century bin economic capital is also elevated, so the 'social only' reading is strongest for 1300-1201 BCE. We therefore interpret the peak as a metallurgical plus monumental-construction phenomenon - prestige copper/gold deposition and collective labour mobilisation - rather than an across-the-board prosperity maximum or a long-distance exchange boom, since amber, the exchange proxy, is decoupled from it. Landscape openness/demography (Belau/Woserin pollen PC1) correlates only weakly (r = 0.02-0.32, n = 36 overlapping bins) and is explicitly not claimed as the mechanism.
native_result.WorkflowB: Read capital.csv with decimal=',' (39 x 100-year bins, BCE positive, no NaN) as the primary grid and sorted chronologically; built SC = ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument (simple sum of raw Z) plus two sensitivity variants (mean of the 3, re-standardised sum); scanned the argmax century with 50/100/150/200/250-year centered rolling means (50y = 2 bins ... 250y = 5 bins) and reported ties explicitly; built a stability table for SC and for the symbolic/cultural/economic blocks. Applied the pre-registered component rule (>=2 of: >=25% of the peak anomaly, delta vs series mean >= +0.5 Z, positive slope over the preceding 500 years) to all 12 components at BOTH tied peak bins, using the exact additive decomposition of the sum for the % of anomaly, and suppressing percentages when a block anomaly was <= +0.5. Compared the four capital blocks under the same sum rule at both tied bins (value, z-score, rank, percentile) to test whether the social peak is specific. Cross-checked the peak on time_series_data.csv using both the 37 raw 100-year anchors (identical to capital.csv, max abs diff 0) and the annual _inter grid with a tie-aware bin comparison. Ran an explicitly secondary pollen check on the 36-bin overlap (4300-800 BCE) against MEAN / Belau_PC1_inter / Woserin_PC1_inter / SMOOTH_MEAN_100y / SMOOTH_MEAN_250y with -200..+200-year lags, using only the fully populated interpolated columns (raw pollen / raw PC1, ~95% NaN, never used). calBP = 1950 - CE_signed. No matplotlib in the environment, so section G prints ASCII panels and writes output/summary.json instead of a PNG.
